chapter: Rose Murphy, wartime 52nd Street, Town Hall
title: Tension between servicemen and musicians at the White Rose Bar
summary: Crouch notes the dangerous area near 50th Street; Stewart saw sailors resent musicians out of uniform, causing scuffles.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah, Dizzy Gillespie mentioned that -- as we were talking about earlier before the interview this morning -- that although 52nd Street itself was integrated and everybody got along pretty well --
Yeah, right.
-- on 52nd Street, that once you hit that strip between 52nd and 50th Street at the -- at where the Radio City Music Hall is at the subway --
Right, that's right.
-- that can be like a very dangerous little area.

Yeah, right. Oh, yes. In fact, a lot of the Army, the sailors and the soldiers, what have you, they used to hang around up and down 52nd Street all around the corner, down to 50th Street, you know, near the subway, and even

in the White Rose Bar, was a very prominent hangout for quite a few of the musicians, you know, in between sets, a lot of sailors and soldiers would come in there and there was a bit of tension in that particular bar between the musicians and the servicemen, you know.
What did the tension arise from?

Well, at times I've noticed -- I did notice that some of the sailors would be -- seem to resent a musician, even standing at the bar drinking, you know, standing right next to him, you know. I saw one incident where one of the musicians, maybe one of the servicemen said something to one of the musicians. There was an argument and the sailor took his hand and the musician had a drink in front of him and took his hand and hit his drink over the bar.
Knocked it off the bar, huh?

Knocked it off the bar, you know. Whatever had been said or done, I think -- I don't know what it was, but I've seen a lot of scuffles happen that way. I've seen that happen quite a few times so whatever that was, that was the tension during those war years, you know.
So like when you saw -- so it was that kind of a situation in which -- now these were white sailors.
Yes, right.
Yeah, okay. So the kind of scuffle that you saw Don Byas have, that was over --
That's right, yeah, sure, right.
-- that was in similar kind of circumstances.

Yeah. There seemed to be a lot of resentment that some of the musicians who weren't in the Service, you might say, walking down and having a good time and everything and the sailors and soldiers, were not in that position -- at least they seemed as though that everything was wrong and wasn't right.
Oh, yeah, that you all weren't doing your duty.
That's right.
Yeah, right. Well, I guess so.
Yes, indeed.
